payload.goal: Make sofar measurably the best work memory for AI coding agents: never below any agent's native memory on any rep, bookkeeping at or below native overhead, and a lead of at least 25-30% (target 2x) on held-out long-horizon, cross-agent, decision-churn work. The lead must survive a native memory that syncs across machines and teammates, so it may never rest on native memory being machine-local.

plan.goal: Make sofar measurably the best work memory for AI coding agents: never below any agent's native memory on any rep, bookkeeping at or below native overhead, and a lead of at least 25-30% (target 2x) on held-out long-horizon, cross-agent, decision-churn work. The lead must survive a native memory that syncs across machines and teammates, so it may never rest on native memory being machine-local.

phases.name: Phase 1 — Wave A: parity at native overhead (ships in 0.33.0-rc.2)

tasks.title: A1 overhead cut: adopt the session from CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID (start_session becomes a fallback), load sofar MCP tools up front (no ToolSearch), a batched end_session taking decisions[]/tasks[]/notes[], task status derived from commits and tests instead of per-subtask update_task. PREDICT (chain A, prompt-matched pairs): store share ≤12% of tool calls on every rep; sofar/automemory cost ≤0.9; retention within ±1 decision. Contract Decisions first (SPEC start_session and end_session).

A2 rule fidelity: a rule stores the operator's quote beside it, the digest renders the quote, and a warning fires when a rule adds status codes, paths or values the quote lacks. PREDICT: claude-sofar S9 and A6 at 100% in 3 of 3 reps.

A3 digest composition: next task's spec first; remember entries surfaced; implementation minutiae dropped from rejected approaches and recent decisions; rules ranked by relevance and rendered last; ≤6k chars. PREDICT: ≤1 raw .sofar read per session; M3 unchanged or better.
rust-core mirrors 1.1–1.3 (hooks, digest render) with conformance parity before rc.2 is pinned

B1 read-time surfacing: when a file is read or edited, the decisions whose guard or derived scope matches it are shown, worded as facts (Claude PostToolUse on Read/Grep, Codex Bash/apply_patch, Cursor postToolUse). PREDICT: C3 re-violation −50%, tokens +<1%.

B2 repo-wide scope and supersession across initiatives: a rule can be app-wide; a reversal of a standing rule in ANY initiative is refused without supersedes (extends L08, which is same-record only). Fixes cursor-sofar's cross-record A2 loss.
B3 executable decision checks with fix hints in the failure, run at Stop, pre-commit and in drive. Blocking needs a Decision revisiting drift-hardening D3 (warn, never block) first.
B4 optional bridge into native memory (repo-local autoMemoryDirectory import, Codex summary), user/feedback types kept local. Needs a privacy Decision first.

phases.name: Phase 3 — Wave C: scale (Rust core, cloud)

tasks.title: Local BM25 index over decisions, rejected approaches and notes, served at prompt time (Rust core); no embeddings without a Decision
Read-time hook under 20 ms at 50+ initiatives and team100 scale (Rust core)
Team decision sync with merge semantics and conflict surfacing through sofar-cloud (fold snapshot contract)

phases.name: Phase 4 — Moat against a cloud-synced native memory

tasks.title: Moat spec: assume Claude Code (and others) ship shared cloud memory; list the advantages that survive: vendor-neutral cross-agent memory, branch- and PR-aware records that merge with the code, typed decisions with supersession and provenance to commits and tests, executable enforcement, deterministic zero-model capture, team governance of rules. Each maps to a benchmark claim with a falsifier.
Retire any public claim or roadmap item whose advantage rests only on native memory being machine-local

Chain L design and budget: ~30 sessions, ~24 planted decisions (guarded, superseded once or twice, why-only), segments across Claude, Codex, fresh clone, concurrent worktrees and a forced compaction. Arms MUST include a native-memory-SYNCED arm (memory dir carried across machines, clones and teammates; Codex idle gate 0) standing in for future cloud memory. Scoped to the D17 cap before authoring.
Author Chain L, hidden tests and a sealed reference by an author blind to fix-building; mutation-validate every planted decision
Round-3 pre-registration frozen with lead predictions (≥25–30%, target 2×) against the synced native arm
Run round 3, report per claim with per-rep values; publish only what clears the pre-registered margin

payload.because: A vendor can remove the machine-local limit with one release. The lasting lead has to come from what a single-vendor, free-form, model-curated memory structurally lacks: memory shared across agents, records that follow git branches and merges, decisions with supersession and provenance, executable enforcement, zero-model capture, and team governance.
payload.chose: Run owner, 2026-09-16 22:40 IST: design against a native memory that syncs across machines and teammates (e.g. Claude shipping shared cloud memory). sofar's lead must hold against that. Every lead claim is benchmarked against a native-memory-SYNCED arm, and no claim or roadmap item may rest on native memory being machine-local.
payload.over: Claiming a lead from fresh-clone, new-machine or teammate scenarios where today's Claude auto memory is absent only because it is machine-local
payload.rule: Never base a sofar lead claim on native memory being machine-local; benchmark every lead against a native-memory arm synced across machines and teammates.

payload.text:
memory-lead 5.1 DESIGN DELIVERED (2026-09-17), per ruling 01M2NQKYPKQDRGN6XM75KA6AZT. Doc: handoff-bench scenario5-launch-bench/analysis/memory-gap-2026-09-16/CHAIN-L-DESIGN.md (uncommitted; design only, no chain content, since handoff-bench is read by engine work).
Shape: 30 sessions, 24 planted decisions (8 guarded, 8 superseded once, 4 twice, 4 why-only), a hidden test per session bound to the version in force. Segments: Claude 1-8; Codex 9-11; fresh clone with empty HOME 12-14; 3 concurrent worktrees 15-17; Cursor 18-20; forced compaction 21-24; Codex 25-27; Claude 28-30. Claude 21 of 30 sessions, so only those bill the D17 cap.
Arms: sofar; native-synced (D1: autoMemoryDirectory carried across every clone, machine and worktree; Codex min_rollout_idle_hours=0 and memories carried; Cursor rules carried); competitor for the D19 gate, chosen by a 3-session screen from Beads/PROJECTMEM/Letta after D14/D15; optional native-local as a covariate only.
Seven claims with falsifiers, all computed against native-synced: decision currency, cross-agent relay, branch and merge, executable checks, why/provenance, cost and overhead, compaction survival. No claim rests on the native store being absent; the fresh-clone segment is a fairness control, not a claim.
Budget on the measured round-1 basis ($3.0-3.6/session chain A, $5.5 assumed for the longer Chain L session; 21 Claude sessions = $115.50 per arm-rep): option A sofar n=3 + native-synced n=3 + competitor n=2 = $924, 2.05 weeks of the $450/7d cap; B = $808 (gate at n=1); C = $1,040 (adds native-local n=1). Full scale, already rejected, is ~$3.3k.
Measurement flags: Claude's background memory extraction may sit outside total_cost_usd and must be counted or reported separately; the Codex 6h idle gate must be 0; compaction summarises hook-added context (a risk measured against sofar, not hidden); hook output caps 10k chars Claude / ~2.5k tokens Codex; every arm on the same Claude system prompt.
Workload: chains A and B spent the Boopada feature list, so Chain L needs its own skeleton. Recommended: a billing/subscription ledger (decision churn is native, invariants are executable, determinism holds).
OWNER RULINGS NEEDED before authoring starts: (1) domain; (2) option A/B/C; (3) competitor screen now or at pre-registration; (4) Cursor has no native memory to sync - keep that segment as a rules comparison or move those 3 sessions to Codex.

payload.note:
The design is delivered and committed at handoff-bench analysis/memory-gap-2026-09-16/CHAIN-L-DESIGN.md (note 01M2NQX7YYAHSSV27F0E9NBE0Q): 30 sessions, 24 decisions, 3 arms (sofar, native-synced, competitor); option A costs $924 of Claude.
Open run-owner rulings: domain, option A/B/C, when to run the competitor screen, and the Cursor segment.
Gap the design misses: the Codex plan limit also binds. There are 6 Codex sessions per arm-rep, so option A needs about 48 Codex sessions, and round 1 hit the limit after about 20 per week. Codex paces Chain L at about 2.5 weeks unless its segments are shortened or its reps trimmed.

payload.because: n=3 on both lead arms is the least that gives an all-reps-agree direction per claim. A billing ledger changes rules naturally (pricing, proration, tax), which is what decision-currency and supersession claims need. Screening competitors before rc.2 and round 2 settle would spend budget on a moving target. Cursor's segment tests relay into a third vendor.
payload.chose:
Chain L rulings (run owner "go", 2026-09-17):
(1) Domain: a billing/subscription ledger.
(2) Option A: sofar n=3, native-synced n=3, competitor n=2; about $924 of Claude, about 2 weeks of the D17 cap.
(3) The competitor screen (Beads, PROJECTMEM, Letta; about $50) runs at round-3 pre-registration, not now.
(4) The Cursor segment stays, compared against carried Cursor rules (Cursor's own recommended store).
Budget amendment: Codex also binds. There are 6 Codex sessions per arm-rep, about 48 in total, against about 20 per Codex week. The author schedules Codex segments across windows or trims Codex reps, and states the plan in the design before authoring.
payload.over: Option B ($808, competitor n=1) or C ($1,040, adds a native-local arm); screening competitors now; dropping the Cursor segment for Codex

payload.text:
memory-lead 5.2 STARTED (2026-09-17). Design amended per ruling 01M2Q79WMSVSR3W587FEGDF3MF: status APPROVED, domain and option A recorded, and the Codex amendment answered in CHAIN-L-DESIGN.md 6.1 — ONE REP PER CAP WINDOW, THREE WINDOWS (18 + 18 + 12 Codex sessions; $346 + $346 + $231 Claude), which clears both the ~20 Codex sessions a week and the $450 cap without trimming any claim. Round 3 therefore spans three windows, about three weeks. Stated fallback (not recommended): cut the second Codex block to 2 sessions, 40 in total over two windows, at the cost of one relay-back session and a weaker L-C2.
Authoring step 2 DONE: the workload skeleton every arm builds from is ~/IO/tallybox-ledger @ e11388d (local, no remote, pre-push refuses). Tallybox is a billing/subscription ledger on the same stack as the Boopada skeleton (Turborepo, bun 1.3, Biome 2.4.10, Next.js 16.1, shadcn/Radix), with NO memory tooling or agent config. packages/providers carries the determinism boundary: catalogue (6 plans, tiered usage components, 4 coupons), customers (8 across US/DE/GB/JP/JO/IN with tax ids and business flags), usage, tax (rates by country, region, category and effective date, including one mid-2027 change and two deliberate gaps), payments (idempotency replay, per-attempt outcomes, expiring card, requires_action) and FX. Provider shapes mirror real billing APIs and never pre-normalise anything a planted decision will decide. build, lint, typecheck and test all pass; 9 provider tests.
Next: the 30 session prompts and 24 planted decisions (sealed, outside handoff-bench), then the sealed reference, then hidden tests with mutation proofs and the three-defect-class audit. No agent will be run against it; round 3 follows round 2.

memory-lead 5.2 progress (2026-09-17), counts and hashes only. Sealed chain-L repo created at ~/IO/bench-sealed/tallybox-chain-l (local, no remote, pre-push refuses), commit fd73244, CHAIN-L.md sha256 308c2e9337c6dec1.
Written so far: the full 24-decision map with its supersession schedule (8 guarded with executable checks, 8 superseded once, 4 superseded twice, 4 why-only probed at the end; 12 of the 24 change under the arm mid-chain), the common footer, and the 8 prompts of the Claude planting segment, which plant 20 of the 24. Verified with the runner's own parser regexes: footer parses, 8 sessions parse, no prompt line over 80 columns.
Still to author: prompts S9-S30 (Codex, fresh clone, three worktrees, Cursor, forced compaction, Codex again, Claude close), then the sealed reference, then hidden tests with a mutation proof per decision version and the three-defect-class audit. E columns in section 1 stay blank until the mutation run fills them.
No agent has been run against any of it.

memory-lead 5.2 progress (2026-09-17): all 30 Chain L session prompts written. Sealed repo ~/IO/bench-sealed/tallybox-chain-l @ 0e80251, CHAIN-L.md sha256 4d4f35f8a3475f28, 738 lines. Counts only, no chain content.
- 30 sessions parse with the runner's own regexes; footer parses; no prompt line over 80 columns.
- 25 sessions carry a decision (planted or superseded); 5 are pure exercise sessions.
- 12 of the 24 decisions change mid-chain, 4 of them twice; every change is stated once, in its own session, and the superseded session's suite is re-run so an arm that kept the old rule is caught.
- Provenance is machine-scored: the why-probe session has its four answers written to a file in the repo, each naming the decision and what was ruled out, instead of being graded from a transcript.
Next: the sealed reference solution, then hidden tests with a mutation proof per decision version, then the three-defect-class audit (unstated clause, state leaking between tests, unspecified numbering), then pins. No agent has been run against any of it.
